newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen steady after ECI data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen steady after ECI data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open firm on Tuesday, taking their cue from bonds after the second quarter employment cost index data matched expectations.
Stocks were also seen buoyed by the U.S. budget and tax accord between President Bill Clinton and Republican leaders.
The Employment Cost Index (ECI), seen as an indicator of inflationary trends, rose 0.8 percent as forecast.

"It's right in line (and) there does not appear to be any surprises. We remain in an environment of moderate growth and benign inflation," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.

Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock and Co said the ECI data was "one of the numbers that was of real concern to Fed watchers. All in all, it's not a bad number and momentum is likely to be stimulated by reaction to the budget deal, which it appears is going to steal the thunder from the data today."
Analysts have said Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan pays close attention to this figure, for signs of upward pressure on wages and benefits.
Monday's historic budget and tax agreement, which aims to balance the budget for the first time since 1969 and cut taxes by $90 billion over the next five years, also underpinned the market.

"The budget deal is a huge bonus," Robert Froelich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds, said. "It could bring a little more focus to cyclical stocks, because to keep a balanced budget in place, the economy has to remain strong."
